headline: High: shared filesystem writes and shared-context skills create medium-to-high risks of leakage, conflict, and cascading errors; prompt injection is limited by lack of direct channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented between argo-workflows and marketingskills, so prompt injection is not default. However, marketingskills explicitly uses shared-context skills and file-based surfaces, while argo-workflows can call APIs and handle artifacts/parameters, so a manual copy-paste or file bridge could carry malicious instructions. The pathway is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF an operator copies marketingskills output into argo-workflows parameters or artifacts
IF a shared file or clipboard bridge is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Require human review before copying text between agents
Strip instruction-like text from shared artifacts
Use a fixed schema for any handoff file

B_data_leakage.rationale: marketingskills has read/write filesystem access and explicit file surfaces, while argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters and has allowlisted network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive artifacts or marketing context can flow from one to the other, and argo-workflows may transmit content onward. The pairwise leakage path is therefore plausible in default-style shared setups.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same workspace or mount the same directory
IF artifacts or marketing context contain sensitive data
mitigations: Separate the filesystem mounts
Disable sharing of raw artifacts between agents
Redact sensitive fields before handoff
Restrict network egress destinations
Audit shared directories for secrets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marketingskills can read and write files and spawn subprocesses, and it supports multiple instances; argo-workflows handles artifacts/parameters and API calls. If both operate on the same mutable workspace or repo, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible. The profiles do not show locking or coordination, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or repository
IF concurrent runs are allowed without external locking
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Serialize runs with a lock file
Disable concurrent instances on shared state
Use read-only mounts for one agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills is designed around shared context and reference-building, so its outputs may be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. argo-workflows can consume artifacts and parameters and then execute workflow steps, making an unverified handoff risky. Because no verification step is documented, the pair can propagate a mistaken marketing claim into downstream actions or reports.
conditions: IF argo-workflows consumes marketingskills output as workflow input
IF no human or schema verification occurs before execution
mitigations: Add a validation step before workflow execution
Require structured outputs with schema checks
Insert human approval for high-impact actions
Log provenance on every handoff

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either argo-workflows or marketingskills, and both profiles are open-source/docs-only. The only concrete compliance-relevant difference is that marketingskills uses filesystem-based skill files while argo-workflows handles artifacts and parameters, which could create policy gaps if sensitive data is introduced. The other agent is not cited because no specific compliance surface is documented.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared skill files or workflow artifacts
IF the deployment environment imposes retention rules on those files
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared files
Set explicit retention on workflow artifacts
Document data-handling responsibilities
Review storage locations for residency requirements
